domain: California Department of Consumer Affairs general laws that bind CSLB contractor licensees (B&P Code general provisions and Division 1): license misuse, address of record, tax/support compliance, citations and fines, cost recovery, court remedies, lawsuits for compensation, settlement agreements, military/veteran licensing, fingerprints
source_doc: 2026 CSLB California Contractors License Law & Reference Book (official), Section V 'The Department of Consumer Affairs', PDF pages 95-156 (B&P Code sections 7.5 through 156); file chunk lawbook_p096-155.txt

rules.title: DCA general laws apply to CSLB licensees
rules.plain_english: CSLB is one of the boards inside the Department of Consumer Affairs, so the general DCA rules in B&P Division 1 (address changes, license misuse, citations, cost recovery, lawsuits for pay, settlement terms) apply to contractors on top of the Contractors License Law.
rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and registrants
rules.verbatim_quote: The department is comprised of the following: ... (j) The Contractors State License Board.
rules.notes: Several sections here say they yield where a board's own licensing act has a specific provision (e.g., B&P 125.3(j), 114.3(g), 115.6(j)); check the CSLB-specific rule in Chapter 9 before applying a DCA default.

rules.title: What counts as a conviction for licensing
rules.plain_english: For licensing, a conviction means a guilty plea or verdict, a no-contest plea, or a finding of guilt. The board can act on it once the appeal time has run, it is upheld on appeal, or probation is granted, but it cannot deny a license to an applicant who is otherwise qualified under B&P 480(b) or (c).

board_may_act_when_any_of: order granting probation suspending imposition of sentence

rules.applies_to: License applicants and licensees with criminal convictions
rules.verbatim_quote: A conviction within the meaning of this code means a judgment following a plea or verdict of guilty or a plea of nolo contendere or finding of guilt. Any action which a board is permitted to take following the establishment of a conviction may be taken when the time for appeal has elapsed, or the judgment of conviction has been affirmed on appeal
rules.notes: The actual denial standards and look-back rules are in B&P 480 (not in this chunk). Do not build a criminal-history eligibility calculator from this section alone.

rules.title: Citations can be issued for regulation violations too
rules.plain_english: Where the code lets the board cite you for breaking a statute, it can also cite you for breaking any regulation adopted under that statute.

citable: violation of regulation adopted under code provision

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: Whenever in any provision of this code authority is granted to issue a citation for a violation of any provision of this code, that authority also includes the authority to issue a citation for the violation of any regulation adopted pursuant to any provision of this code.
rules.notes: CSLB's regulations (California Code of Regulations, Title 16) are therefore citable. A compliance checker should include regulation-level rules, not only statutes.

rules.title: Spouse includes registered domestic partner
rules.plain_english: Wherever the B&P Code says spouse, it also means a registered domestic partner. This matters for the military-spouse licensing rules.
rules.applies_to: Any B&P Code provision using the term spouse
rules.verbatim_quote: “Spouse” includes “registered domestic partner,” as required by Section 297.5 of the Family Code.

rules.title: Definitions of license and licensee
rules.plain_english: A license is any license, certificate, registration, or other authorization to do a regulated business. A licensee is anyone holding one, so the DCA rules reach CSLB registrations (such as home improvement salesperson registrations) as well as contractor licenses.

license_includes: other means to engage in a regulated business or profession

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and registrants
rules.verbatim_quote: Unless otherwise expressly provided, “license” means license, certificate, registration, or other means to engage in a business or profession regulated by this code or referred to in Section 1000 or 3600. ... “Licensee” means any person authorized by a license, certificate, registration, or other means to engage in a business or profession regulated by this code
rules.notes: Several sections (119, 121, 125.6, 152.6) also define license broadly to include permit, authority and registration.

rules.title: Prison rehabilitation training cannot bar licensure
rules.plain_english: Someone trained in a trade through an approved prison rehabilitation program cannot be refused the exam or the license just because of the imprisonment, the conviction behind it, or the fact that the training happened in prison, as long as the board finds them fit.

conditions: training in a rehabilitation program approved by the licensing agency and provided by the prison or institution
licensing agency finds the person fit, upon recommendation of the Adult Authority or Department of the Youth Authority

rules.applies_to: Applicants released from state prison or correctional institutions
rules.verbatim_quote: shall not be denied such license, certificate, or other evidence of proficiency, because of that individual’s imprisonment or the conviction from which the imprisonment resulted, or because the individual obtained the individual’s training in prison ... if the licensing agency ... finds that the individual is a fit person to be licensed.
rules.notes: Relevant for workforce and hiring programs. The fitness finding remains discretionary.

rules.title: License status and enforcement history are public online
rules.plain_english: CSLB must post the status of every license online, including suspensions, revocations, accusations and other enforcement actions, plus information the Labor Commissioner sends it under Labor Code 98.9. Home phone, date of birth and SSN are not posted.

public_online: related enforcement actions including accusations filed under the APA
information provided by the Labor Commissioner under Labor Code 98.9

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and registrants; owners and prime contractors verifying a contractor
rules.verbatim_quote: The Contractors State License Board shall disclose information on its licensees and registrants in accordance with Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 7000) of Division 3. In addition to information related to licenses as specified in subdivision (a), the board shall also disclose information provided to the board by the Labor Commissioner pursuant to Section 98.9 of the Labor Code.
rules.notes: A tool can pull CSLB's online license lookup before contract signing, before each payment, and before hiring subcontractors, and flag suspensions, revocations, accusations or Labor Commissioner items. Labor Code 98.9 is not in this chunk, so what it covers is not described here.

verification.note: Quote and parameters match. B&P 27(c)(6) makes CSLB disclosure "in accordance with Chapter 9", so CSLB-specific disclosure limits in B&P 7124.6 (PDF pages 363-364) also govern, e.g. citations shown for five years after compliance.

rules.title: You may use a P.O. box as your public address of record
rules.plain_english: Your address of record is published, but you may give CSLB a P.O. box or another alternate address instead of your home address. CSLB may still require a physical business or home address for internal use only.

parameters.board_may_require_physical_address: for internal administrative use only, not disclosed

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees, especially sole owners working from home
rules.verbatim_quote: Each entity shall disclose a licensee’s address of record. However, each entity shall allow a licensee to provide a post office box number or other alternate address, instead of the licensee’s home address, as the address of record.
rules.notes: Board notices can be served by regular mail to the last known address (B&P 124), so whatever address you use must be one you actually monitor.

rules.title: Updating legal name or gender on a license
rules.plain_english: If you legally change your name or gender and give the board the required government documents, the board must update your license and its online lookup on request (your former name is not published) and reissue the license for no more than its normal reissue fee. Records of the request are confidential.

name_change_documents_any_of: certified court order under CCP 1277(b) plus copy of Secretary of State Safe at Home certificate
certified court order under CCP 1277.5 or Health and Safety Code 103425 et seq.
gender_change_documents_any_of: state-issued driver’s license or ID card
court order indicating gender change (California, another state, DC, US territory, or foreign court)
parameters.reissue_fee_cap: not higher than the fee regularly charged for reissuing with other updated information

rules.applies_to: Individual licensees and registrants
rules.verbatim_quote: the board, upon request by the licensee or registrant, shall update the individual’s license or registration by replacing references to the former name or gender on the license or registration, as applicable, with references to the current name or gender.
rules.notes: Prior enforcement records under a former name are replaced online by a statement telling the public to contact the board (27.5(a)(2)(B)). After a name change, remember to update the name on contracts, ads and insurance.

rules.title: Child support compliance for issuance and renewal
rules.plain_english: License applicants and renewing licensees must comply with Family Code 17520. If you are not complying with a support judgment or order, your license issuance or renewal is subject to that law.

parameters.trigger: applicant or licensee not in compliance with a judgment or order for support

rules.applies_to: All CSLB applicants and renewing licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: applicants for licensure and licensees renewing their licenses shall also comply with Section 17520 of the Family Code. ... Each applicant for the issuance or renewal of a license, certificate, registration, or other means to engage in a business or profession regulated by a board who is not in compliance with a judgment or order for support shall be subject to Section 17520 of the Family Code.
rules.notes: The consequences under Family Code 17520 (such as license withholding or suspension) are in the Law Book Appendix, not in this chunk.

verification.note: Not a target category; checked because the first quote fragment spans the page 102/103 break. Matches.

rules.title: FEIN, SSN or ITIN required to process a license application
rules.plain_english: When applying, a partnership must give its federal employer identification number, an individual must give an SSN or ITIN, and other applicants an SSN. CSLB will not process an initial application without the number where the application asks for it. These numbers are not public records.

parameters.individual: social security number or individual taxpayer identification number

rules.applies_to: All CSLB license applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: (c) In addition to the penalty specified in subdivision (b), a licensing board shall not process an application for an initial license unless the applicant provides its federal employer identification number, or individual taxpayer identification number or social security number where requested on the application.
rules.notes: An application checklist generator should require the right ID type for each business form. The board shares this data with FTB and EDD on request (30(d)).

rules.title: Failing to provide a tax ID is reported to the FTB
rules.plain_english: A licensee who does not provide the required FEIN, ITIN or SSN is reported to the Franchise Tax Board. If the number still is not provided after the FTB's notice, the licensee faces the penalty in Revenue and Taxation Code 19528(b)(2).

parameters.trigger: failure to provide FEIN/ITIN/SSN, continuing after notification under R&TC 19528(b)(1)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: A licensee failing to provide the federal employer identification number, or the individual taxpayer identification number or social security number shall be reported by the licensing board to the Franchise Tax Board. If the licensee fails to provide that information after notification ... the licensee shall be subject to the penalty
rules.notes: The penalty amount is set in R&TC 19528 and is not stated in this source. Do not assume a figure.

rules.title: Entity licensees must give the SSN or ITIN of every listed person and qualifier
rules.plain_english: When an entity's license is issued, the entity must provide the SSN or ITIN of every individual listed on the license and of anyone who qualifies the license.

ids_required_for: each individual listed on the license
any person who qualifies for the license
parameters.when: at time of issuance of the license

rules.applies_to: Corporations, LLCs, partnerships and other entity contractor licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: a board, as defined in Section 22, the State Bar of California, and the Department of Real Estate shall at the time of issuance of the license require that each licensee provide the individual taxpayer identification number or social security number of each individual listed on the license and any person who qualifies for the license.
rules.notes: In CSLB practice, listed individuals typically include officers, members, partners and the qualifying individual (RMO/RME). That mapping is an interpretation and is not stated in this section.

rules.title: No license denial based on citizenship or immigration status
rules.plain_english: CSLB cannot require you to disclose your citizenship or immigration status and cannot deny a license because of it. An individual may give an ITIN instead of an SSN.

parameters.exception_reference: B&P 7583.23(e) (private security services law, not the Contractors License Law)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB license applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: (B) In implementing the requirements of subparagraph (A), a licensing board shall not require an individual to disclose either citizenship status or immigration status for purposes of licensure. (C) A licensing board shall not deny licensure to an otherwise qualified and eligible individual based solely on the individual’s citizenship status or immigration status.
rules.notes: An application tool should not make citizenship or immigration status a required field.

rules.title: Top-500 state tax delinquents face license suspension
rules.plain_english: If you are on the state's list of the 500 largest tax delinquencies, your license is subject to suspension under B&P 494.5. License applications must state that CDTFA and the FTB can share taxpayer information with the board and that a license may be suspended for unpaid state tax.

parameters.trigger: name appears on list of 500 largest tax delinquencies under R&TC 7063 or 19195
info_sharing_agencies: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: (d) Each licensee or applicant whose name appears on a list of the 500 largest tax delinquencies pursuant to Section 7063 or 19195 of the Revenue and Taxation Code shall be subject to Section 494.5. ... the licensee’s license may be suspended if the state tax obligation is not paid.
rules.notes: R&TC Part 1 covers sales and use tax, Part 10 personal income tax and Part 11 corporation tax. Those labels are general knowledge and are not stated in the source. The B&P 494.5 procedure is not in this chunk.

rules.title: Military training and experience can count toward licensure
rules.plain_english: Board rules must provide a way to evaluate education, training and experience from the U.S. armed services and say how it can count toward license requirements. Every license application must ask whether the applicant is serving or has served in the military.

creditable: experience obtained in the armed services
parameters.application_question_required: is applicant serving in, or has previously served in, the military

rules.applies_to: Contractor license applicants with military service
rules.verbatim_quote: rules and regulations of boards provided for in this code shall provide for methods of evaluating education, training, and experience obtained in the armed services, if applicable to the requirements of the business, occupation, or profession regulated.
rules.notes: CSLB's own rules for crediting experience toward the 4-year experience requirement are in Chapter 9 and its regulations, not in this chunk.

rules.title: Witness fee at board hearings: $12 per day plus expenses
rules.plain_english: A witness who appears at the board's request in a board investigation, proceeding or hearing may be paid $12 per day of attendance plus actual, necessary and reasonable expenses. Witnesses appearing for another party are not paid from the board's fund.
rules.applies_to: Homeowners, contractors or others testifying in CSLB proceedings
rules.verbatim_quote: any witness appearing at the investigation, proceeding, or hearing whether upon a subpoena or voluntarily, may be paid the sum of twelve dollars ($12) per day for every day in actual attendance at the investigation, proceeding, or hearing and for the witness’s actual, necessary, and reasonable expenses
rules.notes: The statute says may be paid, so payment is discretionary.

rules.title: Reinstating a license that expired during active military duty
rules.plain_english: If your license expired while you were on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces or California National Guard, you can reinstate it without an exam or penalty. The license must have been valid when you entered service, you must apply while serving or within 1 year of discharge, and you must file an affidavit of your service dates and pay the current renewal fee.

parameters.window: while serving, or not later than 1 year from discharge from active service or return to inactive military status
parameters.window_trigger: date of discharge from active service or return to inactive status
required_documents: affidavit showing date of entrance into service, whether still serving, or date of discharge
renewal fee for the current renewal period
exam_may_be_required_if: filed more than 1 year after discharge or return to inactive status
board finds applicant did not actively practice the profession while on active duty
parameters.excluded_from_1_year_period: time in treatment or hospitalization in a veterans’ facility that prevented practice

rules.applies_to: Licensees whose licenses expired during active military service
rules.verbatim_quote: may, upon application, reinstate their license or registration without examination or penalty, provided that ... (2) The application for reinstatement is made while serving in the California National Guard or the United States Armed Forces, or not later than one year from the date of discharge from active service or return to inactive military status.
rules.notes: A deadline calculator should compute discharge date + 1 year, extended by any documented veterans' facility treatment time.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 122, 124 (B&P 114(a)-(c) and final paragraph; B&P 115)

rules.title: Keep your license current if you work in California while in the military
rules.plain_english: If you do licensed work in California, part time or full time, while in military service, you must keep your license in good standing.

parameters.trigger: practicing the licensed vocation in California part time or full time while in military service

rules.applies_to: Licensees in military service who continue contracting in California
rules.verbatim_quote: any licensee or registrant who, either part time or full time, practices in this state the profession or vocation for which the licensee or registrant is licensed or registered shall be required to maintain their license in good standing even though the licensee or registrant is in military service.
rules.notes: Applies unless the code specifically provides otherwise.

rules.title: Renewal fee and requirement waiver while on active duty
rules.plain_english: If you are called to active duty, the board waives renewal fees, continuing education and other renewal requirements for the active-duty period. Your license must have been current when you were called up, and you must give written proof of service. While the waiver is in effect you may not do licensed work, except under a military active status with no private practice.

conditions: current and valid license when called to active duty
written documentation substantiating active duty service
waived: other renewal requirements as determined by the board
parameters.exception: license converted to military active status if providing services while on active duty; no private practice of any type
parameters.active_duty_definition: 10 USC 101 plus California National Guard active duty under Mil. & Vet. Code 143 or 146

rules.applies_to: Licensees called to active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces or California National Guard
rules.verbatim_quote: every board ... within the department shall waive the renewal fees, continuing education requirements, and other renewal requirements as determined by the board, if any are applicable, for a licensee or registrant called to active duty ... the licensee or registrant shall not engage in any activities requiring a license during the period that the waivers provided by this section are in effect.
rules.notes: Under 114.3(g) this section does not apply to a board that has its own statutory renewal waiver process. Verify whether CSLB has one in Chapter 9.

rules.title: After discharge: notify within 60 days, renew within 6 months
rules.plain_english: After you get notice of your discharge date, tell the board within 60 days. Before doing licensed work again, meet all renewal requirements within 6 months of your discharge date.

parameters.notify_trigger: receipt of notice of discharge date
parameters.renewal_trigger: date of discharge from active duty service

rules.applies_to: Licensees who used the B&P 114.3 active-duty waiver
rules.verbatim_quote: shall meet all necessary renewal requirements as determined by the board within six months from the licensee’s or registrant’s date of discharge from active duty service. ... shall notify the board of their discharge from active duty within 60 days of receiving their notice of discharge.
rules.notes: Two calculable deadlines: notice receipt + 60 days, and discharge date + 6 months. B&P 114.3(g): the section does not apply to a board with a similar statutory renewal-waiver process. CSLB B&P 7071.3 (designating a responsible managing person while in the armed forces, renewal fee still paid) is not such a waiver.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 123-124 (B&P 114.3(d)-(e), (g) and history note)
verification.note: 60-day notice and 6-month renewal periods confirmed. B&P 114.3(g) says the section does not apply to a board with its own statutory renewal-waiver process. CSLB B&P 7071.3 (PDF page 291) is not a waiver: it lets a licensee entering the armed forces name a responsible managing person, and the renewal fee must still be paid. So 114.3 appears to apply to CSLB, but that is an inference.

rules.title: Expedited initial licensure for veterans and SkillBridge members
rules.plain_english: CSLB must expedite initial licensing for applicants who show they were honorably discharged after active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces, and since July 1, 2024 for active-duty members enrolled in the DoD SkillBridge program. This applies only to individual licenses, not business or entity licenses.

eligible_groups.group: honorably discharged former active duty members of the U.S. Armed Forces
active duty members of a regular component enrolled in DoD SkillBridge (10 USC 1143(e))

parameters.required_evidence: satisfactory evidence of service and honorable discharge, or SkillBridge enrollment
parameters.license_scope: individual license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Veteran and SkillBridge applicants for an individual license
rules.verbatim_quote: on and after July 1, 2016, a board within the department shall expedite, and may assist, the initial licensure process for an applicant who supplies satisfactory evidence to the board that the applicant has served as an active duty member of the Armed Forces of the United States and was honorably discharged.
rules.effective: July 1, 2016; SkillBridge from July 1, 2024 (amended effective September 22, 2024)
rules.notes: The section states no fee waiver. How 'individual license' maps to CSLB sole-owner versus entity licenses is not stated, so verify with CSLB.

rules.title: Military spouses: expedited license with application and initial fees waived
rules.plain_english: CSLB must expedite licensing and waive both the application fee and the initial license fee for an applicant who is married to (or a domestic partner of) an active-duty service member stationed in California under orders, and who holds a current license for the same trade in another state or U.S. territory.

parameters.waived_fee_usd: full amount of the listed fees
conditions: married to, domestic partner of, or in another legal union with an active duty U.S. Armed Forces member assigned to a California duty station under official orders
holds a current license in another U.S. state, district, or territory in the same profession or vocation
parameters.license_scope: individual license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Military-spouse applicants for an individual contractor license
rules.verbatim_quote: A board within the department shall expedite the licensure process and waive the licensure application fee and the initial or original license fee charged by the board for an applicant who meets both of the following requirements:
rules.effective: Operative July 1, 2021 version as amended effective September 22, 2024
rules.notes: A fee calculator should set the application and initial license fees to $0 for qualifying applicants. Renewal fees are not waived by this section.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 125 (B&P 115.5(a)-(c), operative version)
verification.note: Fee waiver and conditions confirmed. The book history note says the current version is "operative July 1, 2021", but the predecessor was "Repealed July 1, 2022". The 2021 date may be a typo in the book for July 1, 2022. The source alone cannot resolve this.

rules.title: Temporary license for military spouses: issued in 30 days, valid 12 months, no fee
rules.plain_english: A spouse or domestic partner of an active-duty member stationed in California who holds an active, unrestricted out-of-state license with the same scope can get a free, nonrenewable temporary license. The board must issue it within 30 days of complete documents if the background check is clean, and it expires after 12 months or when a regular license is issued or denied, whichever comes first.

parameters.issue_trigger: receipt of documentation meeting 115.6(c) and (d), with criminal background check showing no grounds for denial
expires_at_earliest_of: issuance or denial of standard license
issuance or denial of license by endorsement
issuance or denial of expedited license under 115.5
required_documents: evidence of marriage, domestic partnership or legal union with an active duty member assigned to a California duty station under official orders
current, active, unrestricted out-of-state license within the same scope
application with signed affidavit of eligibility and accuracy
written verification of good standing from original licensing jurisdiction
full set of fingerprints on request
disqualifiers: act in any jurisdiction that would be grounds for denial, suspension or revocation
discipline by a licensing entity in another jurisdiction
unresolved complaint, review procedure or disciplinary proceeding in another jurisdiction
parameters.exam_required: California law and ethics exam only if otherwise required by the board
parameters.termination: may be terminated immediately for failing requirements or inaccurate information; holder must cease practice immediately on receipt of notice
parameters.license_scope: individual license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Military-spouse applicants holding an out-of-state contractor license
rules.verbatim_quote: a board shall issue a temporary license pursuant to this section within 30 days of receiving documentation that the applicant has met the requirements ... A temporary license issued pursuant to this section is nonrenewable and shall expire 12 months after issuance
rules.notes: Under 115.6(j) this section does not apply to a board that already has an expedited temporary authorization (at least 1 year) or endorsement process. Verify CSLB's status.

verification.note: Not a target category; numeric terms checked: 30 days to issue (e), 12-month nonrenewable term (h), no fee (k). Under 115.6(j)(1) the section does not apply to a board with its own expedited temporary-authorization or endorsement process for military spouses.

rules.title: Registration for servicemembers and spouses relocated on military orders
rules.plain_english: A servicemember or spouse who moved to California on military orders and holds a good-standing out-of-state license for similar work can register with the board for free, if they performed at least one licensed activity in the 2 years before relocating. The board must register them within 30 days of complete documents, and the registration ends when the orders expire.

parameters.register_trigger: receipt of all applicable documentation under 115.10(b)
required_documents: copy of military orders for service in California
written verification or online printout of good standing from original licensing jurisdiction
good-standing verification for each jurisdiction if licensed in more than one
evidence of marriage, domestic partnership or legal union (spouse applicants)
publicly_posted: state name and license number of each original license
parameters.license_scope: individual professional license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Servicemembers and spouses relocated to California under military orders
rules.verbatim_quote: (3) The applicant performed at least one activity within the scope and under the authority of their professional license during the two years immediately preceding the relocation to this state. ... (c) (1) The registering authority shall register an applicant within 30 days of receiving all applicable documentation described in subdivision (b).
rules.notes: The board can revoke or suspend the registration for not meeting requirements. How CSLB applies this to contractor classifications is not stated here, so verify.

verification.note: Not a target category; numeric terms checked: 30 days to register (c)(1), 2-year activity lookback (b)(3), no fee (g). Quote matches across the margin text.

rules.title: Withdrawing an application or letting a license lapse does not stop discipline
rules.plain_english: Withdrawing a license application does not stop the board from denying it unless the board agrees in writing. A license that is suspended, expired, forfeited, cancelled, or surrendered without the board's written consent can still be disciplined during any period when it could be renewed, restored or reinstated.

events_that_do_not_end_jurisdiction: suspension, forfeiture or cancellation by board or court order
surrender without written consent of board
parameters.jurisdiction_period: any period in which the license may be renewed, restored, reissued, or reinstated

rules.applies_to: CSLB applicants and licensees facing complaints or discipline
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) The suspension, expiration, or forfeiture by operation of law of a license issued by a board in the department, or its suspension, forfeiture, or cancellation by order of the board or by order of a court of law, or its surrender without the written consent of the board, shall not, during any period in which it may be renewed, restored, reissued, or reinstated, deprive the board
rules.notes: The renewal or reinstatement window for CSLB licenses is set in Chapter 9 (not in this chunk).

rules.title: Misdemeanor to display an invalid, fake, borrowed or copied license
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor to display or possess a cancelled, revoked, suspended or altered license or a fake license, to present someone else's license as your own, to copy a license so it could pass as valid, or to knowingly buy or receive a forged license.

prohibited_acts: displaying, permitting display of, or possessing a canceled, revoked, suspended, or fraudulently altered license
displaying or possessing a fictitious license or document simulating a license
displaying or representing a license not issued to the person as their own
photographing, duplicating or reproducing a license so it could be mistaken for a valid license, or displaying or possessing such a reproduction, unless authorized
buying or receiving a fraudulent, forged or counterfeited license knowingly

rules.applies_to: Any person, licensed or not, including contractors, salespersons and subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Displays or causes or permits to be displayed or has in the person’s possession either of the following: (1) A canceled, revoked, suspended, or fraudulently altered license. (2) A fictitious license or any document simulating a license or purporting to be or have been issued as a license. ... (c) Displays or represents any license not issued to the person as being the person’s license.
rules.notes: A tool can block printing the license number or license image on bids, contracts, trucks or websites when the CSLB status is not active, and can flag subcontractors whose displayed license number does not match their own name.

rules.title: Never lend your license or let others use it
rules.plain_english: Lending your license to anyone, or knowingly letting another person use it or use it unlawfully, is a misdemeanor.

prohibited_acts: lending license to any other person
knowingly permitting use of license by another
knowingly permitting any unlawful use of a license issued to the person

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees (individual and entity)
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person who does any of the following is guilty of a misdemeanor: ... (b) Lends the person’s license to any other person or knowingly permits the use thereof by another. ... (e) Knowingly permits any unlawful use of a license issued to the person.
rules.notes: See also B&P 125 (aiding unlicensed persons). Chapter 9 contains contractor-specific license-lending and aiding rules (not in this chunk).

rules.title: Surrender a suspended or revoked license when demanded in writing
rules.plain_english: If your license, registration or permit is suspended, revoked or cancelled and the board demands it in writing, you must surrender it. Failing or refusing is a misdemeanor.

parameters.trigger: lawful written demand by issuing authority

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees whose license is suspended, revoked or cancelled
rules.verbatim_quote: (d) Fails or refuses to surrender to the issuing authority upon its lawful written demand any license, registration, permit, or certificate which has been suspended, revoked, or canceled.
rules.notes: No surrender deadline is stated in this section. Treat the deadline in the board's written demand as controlling.

rules.title: Renew before expiration and you are legal while you wait for the new card
rules.plain_english: If you complete your renewal before the license expires, you are not working illegally while you wait for proof of renewal, as long as the delay is not your fault. That period also counts as licensed for the rule on suing for payment.

parameters.condition: renewal requirements complied with before license expiration
parameters.protected_period: between renewal and receipt of evidence of renewal

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees renewing a license
rules.verbatim_quote: No licensee who has complied with the provisions of this code relating to the renewal of the licensee’s license prior to expiration of such license shall be deemed to be engaged illegally in the practice of the licensee’s business or profession during any period between such renewal and receipt of evidence of such renewal which may occur due to delay not the fault of the applicant.
rules.notes: A license tracker should push renewal before the expiration date and keep proof of the submission date (e.g., a mailing or online receipt). A renewal submitted after expiration gets no protection under this section.

verification.note: B&P 121 quote matches; the automated match missed only because of a page break. B&P 143(c) says 143 does not apply to acts that are lawful practice under 121. For contractors, suits for compensation are mainly governed by B&P 7031 in Chapter 9.

rules.title: No delinquency fees on lawfully inactive or retired licenses
rules.plain_english: Delinquency fees and back renewal fees for expired licenses do not apply to a license that was lawfully placed in inactive or retired status, unless the code says otherwise.

parameters.exception: as otherwise provided in this code

rules.applies_to: Licensees with inactive or retired licenses
rules.verbatim_quote: Except as otherwise provided in this code, the application of delinquency fees or accrued and unpaid renewal fees for the renewal of expired licenses or registrations shall not apply to licenses or registrations that have lawfully been designated as inactive or retired.
rules.notes: CSLB inactive-license fees and rules are in Chapter 9 (B&P 7076.5 and related). Verify the amounts there.

rules.title: Duplicate license certificate fee: max $25
rules.plain_english: The fee to get a duplicate copy of your license certificate or renewal evidence cannot exceed $25, unless another law provides otherwise.

parameters.exception: except as otherwise provided by law

rules.applies_to: Licensees requesting a duplicate license certificate or pocket card
rules.verbatim_quote: The fee shall be in an amount sufficient to cover all costs incident to the issuance of the duplicate certificate or other form but shall not exceed twenty-five dollars ($25).
rules.notes: CSLB's actual duplicate fee may be set in Chapter 9 or regulations. Use the CSLB fee schedule for actual amounts, capped at $25 under this section absent another law. Verified: B&P 7137(a)(6)(D) fixes the CSLB fee for a duplicate certificate of licensure or renewal evidence "pursuant to Section 122" at $25 (PDF page 377).

verification.note: $25 cap confirmed. CSLB fee statute B&P 7137(a)(6)(D) (PDF page 377) sets the CSLB duplicate-certificate fee at exactly $25.

rules.title: Cheating on the license exam: misdemeanor plus up to $10,000 in damages
rules.plain_english: Compromising a license exam, for example by removing or copying exam materials, using paid test-takers to reconstruct it, copying from or communicating with other examinees, bringing unauthorized notes, or using an impersonator, is a misdemeanor. The violator is also liable for the exam agency's actual damages up to $10,000 plus litigation costs, and a court can enjoin the conduct.
rules.applies_to: Contractor license exam candidates and exam-prep providers
rules.verbatim_quote: In addition to any other penalties, a person found guilty of violating this section, shall be liable for the actual damages sustained by the agency administering the examination not to exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000) and the costs of litigation.
rules.notes: This also reaches exam-prep schools that sell or use leaked exam questions (123(a)).

verification.note: Quote matches across the page 133/134 break. Misdemeanor, up to $10,000 actual damages plus litigation costs, and injunction on application of a board, the AG or the DA are all confirmed.

rules.title: Board notices can be served by regular mail to your last known address
rules.plain_english: Board notices, orders and documents, including disciplinary accusations and decisions, may be served by regular mail to your last known address or by personal service, at the board's choice. Mail sent to an outdated address still counts.

service_methods: regular mail addressed to last known address of the licensee
covers: notices, orders and documents under Gov. Code 11340+, 11370+ and 11500+ (APA)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: the notice may be given by regular mail addressed to the last known address of the licensee or by personal service, at the option of the board.
rules.notes: Combined with the 30-day address-change rule (B&P 136), this means deadlines such as the 30-day citation appeal can start running on mail you never saw. A tool should keep the address of record current and watched.

verification.note: Statute text confirmed. "Mail sent to an outdated address still counts" is an inference from "last known address", not stated words. CSLB citations under B&P 7099 must be contested within 15 days after service (B&P 7099.8(a), PDF page 342), not 30 days.

rules.title: Helping an unlicensed person: misdemeanor plus discipline
rules.plain_english: A licensee who conspires with an unlicensed person to violate the code, or who helps them by letting them use the license or by acting as their agent or partner, commits a misdemeanor and can be disciplined.

prohibited_acts: conspiring with an unlicensed person to violate the code
allowing license to be used by an unlicensed person with intent to aid their violation
acting as agent or partner of an unlicensed person with intent to aid their violation

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees, e.g., a licensed contractor fronting for an unlicensed operator
rules.verbatim_quote: is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to the disciplinary provisions of this code applicable to them, who conspires with a person not so licensed to violate any provision of this code, or who, with intent to aid or assist that person in violating those provisions does either of the following: (a) Allows their license to be used by that person. (b) Acts as their agent or partner.
rules.notes: Chapter 9 has contractor-specific aiding and abetting rules (e.g., B&P 7114, not in this chunk).

rules.title: Disciplined licensees can be ordered to pay investigation and enforcement costs
rules.plain_english: If you are found to have violated the licensing law in a disciplinary case, the judge can order you to pay the board's reasonable investigation and enforcement costs up to the hearing date, including Attorney General charges. For a corporation or partnership the order can be made against the licensed entity, and the board can enforce it in court.

parameters.max_amount: reasonable costs of investigation and enforcement of the case
parameters.cost_period: up to the date of the hearing
parameters.entity_liability: licensed corporation or partnership may be ordered to pay
parameters.prima_facie_evidence: certified copy of actual costs, or good-faith estimate, signed by entity bringing the proceeding

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees in formal disciplinary proceedings
rules.verbatim_quote: the administrative law judge may direct a licensee found to have committed a violation or violations of the licensing act to pay a sum not to exceed the reasonable costs of the investigation and enforcement of the case.
rules.notes: Under 125.3(j) this section does not apply if the board's own licensing act has a specific cost-recovery provision. Verify for CSLB in Chapter 9. Verified: CSLB B&P 7095(b)(2) expressly allows cost payment "pursuant to Section 125.3" as a disciplinary term, so 125.3 applies to CSLB.

verification.note: Confirmed. On the 125.3(j) carve-out: CSLB B&P 7095(b)(2) (PDF page 338) lists "Payment of the costs of investigation and enforcement pursuant to Section 125.3" as a permitted decision term. CSLB therefore uses 125.3, and no separate CSLB cost-recovery statute was found.

rules.title: Unpaid cost-recovery orders block renewal (1-year hardship plan possible)
rules.plain_english: The board will not renew or reinstate your license until you pay all costs ordered against you. If you show financial hardship and sign a formal agreement to repay within one year, the board may conditionally renew or reinstate for up to one year.

hardship_conditions: formal agreement to reimburse board within the one-year period

rules.applies_to: Licensees with unpaid cost-recovery orders
rules.verbatim_quote: (g) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), the board shall not renew or reinstate the license of any licensee who has failed to pay all of the costs ordered under this section. (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the board may, in its discretion, conditionally renew or reinstate for a maximum of one year the license of any licensee who demonstrates financial hardship
rules.notes: A renewal-readiness checker should flag outstanding cost orders before the renewal date.

rules.title: Court injunctions and restitution to injured consumers
rules.plain_english: On a board petition approved by the DCA Director, the superior court can stop anyone, licensed or not, from violating the licensing law and order them to pay restitution to the people harmed. The court can also make them repay the board's investigation expenses.

parameters.court: superior court of the county where the violation occurred or is about to occur
parameters.petitioner: board, with approval of the Director
remedies: restitution to persons injured by the violation

rules.applies_to: Licensed and unlicensed contractors; injured homeowners as beneficiaries
rules.verbatim_quote: The superior court for the county in which any person has engaged in any act which constitutes a violation of a chapter of this code administered or enforced by a board within the department may, upon a petition filed by the board with the approval of the director, order such person to make restitution to persons injured as a result of such violation.
rules.notes: This remedy is in addition to other remedies in the code (125.5(d)).

verification.note: Quote is from 125.5(b) and matches across the page break.

rules.title: No refusing or limiting service because of protected characteristics
rules.plain_english: A licensee can be disciplined for refusing to do licensed work, restricting or discriminating in how it is done, or getting another licensee to refuse, because of any characteristic protected by Civil Code 51(b) or (e). Architectural barriers that meet applicable building codes are not discrimination under this section, and it does not cover employer-employee discrimination.

prohibited_acts: refusing to perform the licensed activity
aiding or inciting another licensee's refusal
discrimination or restriction in performance of the licensed activity
not_covered: employer discrimination regarding employees or prospective employees
parameters.safe_harbor: architectural barriers conforming to applicable state or local building codes and regulations

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees in dealing with customers (applicants for licensed services)
rules.verbatim_quote: every person who holds a license under the provisions of this code is subject to disciplinary action ... if, because of any characteristic listed or defined in subdivision (b) or (e) of Section 51 of the Civil Code, the person refuses to perform the licensed activity or aids or incites the refusal to perform that licensed activity by another licensee
rules.notes: Civil Code 51 is the Unruh Civil Rights Act (general knowledge; the list of characteristics is not reproduced in this source). Employment discrimination is governed by other law.

rules.title: Court order barring a contractor from working: accusation within 30 days, hearing within 30 days
rules.plain_english: A court can temporarily bar a contractor from working if letting them continue would endanger public health, safety or welfare. The board must file an accusation within 30 days of the order. If the contractor requests a hearing, the board must hold it within 30 days and decide within 15 days after it ends, or the court may cancel the order.

parameters.standard: continuing to engage in the business will endanger public health, safety, or welfare
parameters.without_notice_only_if: affidavits show serious injury to the public before the matter can be heard on notice
parameters.consequence_of_board_delay: court may nullify the restraining order
parameters.dissolves: when the board's decision becomes subject to judicial review under CCP 1094.5

rules.applies_to: Division 3 licensees, which include CSLB contractors (Chapter 9 is in Division 3)
rules.verbatim_quote: in any case not more than 30 days after the restraining order is issued, an accusation shall be filed with the board ... if the licensee requests a hearing on the accusation, the board must provide the licensee with a hearing within 30 days of the request and a decision within 15 days of the date of the conclusion of the hearing, or the court may nullify the restraining order previously issued.
rules.notes: B&P 125.7 (a similar procedure) applies to Division 2 healing-arts licensees, not contractors, and was omitted.

verification.note: Not a target category; checked. B&P 125.8(d) on page 140: accusation within 30 days, hearing within 30 days of request, decision within 15 days of the hearing's conclusion. The similar text on page 139 is B&P 125.7 (decision within 15 days of receipt of the ALJ decision) and does not govern contractors. 125.8 covers Division 3 licensees, which includes Chapter 9 contractors.

rules.title: What a citation must contain
rules.plain_english: A citation must be in writing, describe the violation in detail, and cite the specific law violated. Where appropriate it includes an order of abatement with a reasonable time to fix the problem. A citation may be issued with or without a fine.

must_include: particular description of the nature of the violation
specific reference to the provision of law violated
parameters.include_when_appropriate: order of abatement fixing a reasonable time for abatement

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees receiving citations
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Citations shall be in writing and shall describe with particularity the nature of the violation, including specific reference to the provision of law determined to have been violated. (2) Whenever appropriate, the citation shall contain an order of abatement fixing a reasonable time for abatement of the violation.
rules.notes: This is the general DCA citation framework. CSLB has its own citation provisions in Chapter 9 (B&P 7099 et seq., not in this chunk), which control for contractors where they differ.

verification.note: Confirmed. 125.9(c) items (a citation without a fine, fines limited to particular violations) are optional ("The system may contain"). The 125.9 system exists only where a board adopts it by regulation (125.9(a)). CSLB B&P 7099 (PDF page 339) has a parallel requirement: written, particular description and the provisions violated, with an optional order of correction or civil penalty.

rules.title: DCA default citation fine cap: $5,000
rules.plain_english: Under the general DCA citation system, a fine cannot exceed $5,000 per inspection or investigation, or $5,000 per violation or count for fraudulent billing to an insurer, Medi-Cal or Medicare. The amount must reflect the gravity of the violation, the licensee's good faith and any prior violations.
rules.applies_to: Licensees cited under a board's B&P 125.9 citation system
rules.verbatim_quote: In no event shall the administrative fine assessed by the board, bureau, or commission exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000) for each inspection or each investigation made with respect to the violation, or five thousand dollars ($5,000) for each violation or count if the violation involves fraudulent billing submitted to an insurance company, the Medi-Cal program, or Medicare.
rules.notes: CSLB issues contractor citations under its own Chapter 9 provisions (B&P 7099 et seq.), which may set different maximums. Do not use $5,000 as the CSLB contractor cap without checking Chapter 9. Verified CSLB override: B&P 7099.2, operative July 1, 2026, "Notwithstanding Section 125.9": civil penalty $500-$8,000, or $1,500-$30,000 for B&P 7110, 7114, 7118 violations. Minimums are CPI-adjustable every 5 years (PDF page 340).

verification.note: The $5,000 DCA default is confirmed. CSLB override verified: B&P 7099.2, operative July 1, 2026 (PDF page 340), applies "Notwithstanding Section 125.9". CSLB civil penalties are $500 to $8,000, and $1,500 to $30,000 for violations of B&P 7110, 7114 or 7118. Minimums may be inflation-adjusted every five years. The pre-July 2026 version had an $8,000 maximum, or $30,000 for those sections, with no minimum.

rules.title: DCA-default (B&P 125.9) citations: request a hearing in writing within 30 days of issuance (CSLB B&P 7099 citations: 15 days from service)
rules.plain_english: Under the general DCA citation system in B&P 125.9, the citation must tell you that a hearing to contest it must be requested by written notice to the board within 30 days of the date the citation or fine assessment was issued. Paying a fine without requesting a hearing is not an admission of the violation. This 30-day window does not govern ordinary CSLB contractor citations, which are issued under B&P 7099. To contest those, file a written request for an administrative hearing, or for an informal citation conference, within 15 days after service of the citation (B&P 7099.8(a)-(b), "notwithstanding any other law"). B&P 7099.3 and 7099.4 say 15 working days, extendable by the registrar for cause. If you do not contest in time, the citation becomes a final order not subject to review.

parameters.trigger: date of issuance of the citation or assessment

cslb_7099_citation_contest.method: written request for administrative hearing (B&P 7028.12/7099.5) and/or written request for informal citation conference to the chief of the enforcement division
cslb_7099_citation_contest.alt_statement: B&P 7099.3/7099.4: 15 working days from service; registrar may extend for cause
cslb_7099_citation_contest.after_informal_conference: contest affirmed/modified citation by written hearing request within 30 days after its service (B&P 7099.8(b)(4))
cslb_7099_citation_contest.if_not_contested: citation deemed a final order of the registrar, not subject to review by any court or agency (B&P 7099.4)

rules.applies_to: Licensees cited under a board's B&P 125.9 citation system. Not CSLB citations issued under B&P 7099; see cslb_7099_citation_contest.
rules.verbatim_quote: if the licensee desires a hearing to contest the finding of a violation, that hearing shall be requested by written notice to the board, bureau, or commission within 30 days of the date of issuance of the citation or assessment. If a hearing is not requested pursuant to this section, payment of any fine shall not constitute an admission of the violation charged.
rules.notes: Deadline under 125.9 runs from issuance, not receipt. CSLB contractor citations are issued under B&P 7099 and follow the shorter 15-day-from-service rule in B&P 7099.8. Use 15 days from service for CSLB citations. Use 30 days from issuance only for a citation expressly issued under a B&P 125.9 system.

verification.correction: The 125.9(b)(4) quote and its 30-day period are accurate. But the title and plain English presented 30 days as the contractor's window to contest a citation. CSLB contractor citations under B&P 7099 must be contested within 15 days after service (B&P 7099.8(a), "notwithstanding any other law"; 7099.3/7099.4 say 15 working days), and the trigger is service, not issuance. Rescoped title, plain_english and applies_to, and added parameters.cslb_7099_citation_contest.

rules.title: DCA-default (B&P 125.9) citations: pay and abate within 30 days or face discipline and a blocked renewal (CSLB B&P 7099 citations: automatic suspension under B&P 7090.1)
rules.plain_english: Under the general DCA citation system in B&P 125.9, unless you are appealing, you must pay the fine and comply with any abatement order within 30 days of the assessment or order, or face possible discipline. An uncontested, unpaid fine is added to your renewal fee, and the license will not be renewed until both are paid. For CSLB contractor citations under B&P 7099, B&P 7090.1 applies instead. Once the citation is final, failing to pay the civil penalty or comply with the order of correction (or the order to pay an injured party) automatically suspends the license by operation of law 30 days after noncompliance. The registrar sends written notice that the license will be suspended 30 days from the notice date, and you may contest the noncompliance finding in writing within 15 days after service of that notice. If the license is not reinstated within 90 days of the automatic suspension, the cited license and any other contractor license issued to you are automatically revoked. The registrar may delay revocation for good cause for up to 1 year, on written request made before revocation. You are also barred from serving as an officer or qualifier of another licensee.

consequences: uncontested unpaid fine added to license renewal fee
license not renewed without payment of renewal fee and fine

cslb_7090_1_noncompliance.trigger: failure to pay civil penalty or comply with order of correction / order to pay injured party once the citation order is final
cslb_7090_1_noncompliance.registrar_notice: written notice that license will be suspended 30 days from date of notice
cslb_7090_1_noncompliance.revocation_scope: cited license and any other contractors license issued to the licensee
cslb_7090_1_noncompliance.reinstatement: at any time after suspension by complying with the final order
cslb_7090_1_noncompliance.collateral: automatically prohibited from serving as officer, director, associate, partner, manager or qualifier of another licensee; other licensee must replace a disassociated qualifier within 90 days

rules.applies_to: Licensees cited under a board's B&P 125.9 citation system. CSLB citations under B&P 7099 follow B&P 7090.1; see cslb_7090_1_noncompliance.
rules.verbatim_quote: Failure of a licensee to pay a fine or comply with an order of abatement, or both, within 30 days of the date of assessment or order, unless the citation is being appealed, may result in disciplinary action ... Where a citation is not contested and a fine is not paid, the full amount of the assessed fine shall be added to the fee for renewal of the license.
rules.notes: For CSLB citations, calendar the 7090.1 dates: 30 days to automatic suspension, a 15-day window to contest the noncompliance notice, and 90 days from suspension to automatic revocation. The 125.9 30-day rule is the DCA default only.

verification.correction: The 125.9(b)(5) quote and parameters are accurate. But the rule presented the 30-day pay/abate consequence (possible discipline, fine added to renewal) as the contractor rule. CSLB citations under B&P 7099 are governed by B&P 7090.1 (PDF pages 335-336): automatic suspension 30 days after noncompliance with the final order, 15 days to contest the noncompliance notice, and automatic revocation if not reinstated within 90 days. Rescoped title, plain_english and applies_to, and added parameters.cslb_7090_1_noncompliance.

rules.title: A paid and abated citation is disclosed as satisfactorily resolved
rules.plain_english: If you pay the fine and comply with any abatement order, the public record must show the matter as satisfactorily resolved.

conditions: order of abatement complied with, if applicable

rules.applies_to: Cited licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: if a fine is paid to satisfy an assessment based on the finding of a violation, payment of the fine and compliance with the order of abatement, if applicable, shall be represented as satisfactory resolution of the matter for purposes of public disclosure.
rules.notes: How long CSLB keeps citations on its public website is set in Chapter 9 or regulations, not here. Verified: B&P 7124.6(e)(1)(A) (PDF pages 363-364) has CSLB citations disclosed from issuance until 5 years after compliance, if no further disciplinary actions are filed in that period.

verification.note: Confirmed. CSLB disclosure period verified in B&P 7124.6(e)(1)(A): citations are disclosed from issuance until five years after compliance if no additional disciplinary actions are filed in that period.

rules.title: Selling supplies or services to someone you know is unlicensed: misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor to sell equipment, supplies or services to anyone when you know they will be used for work or a contract that violates licensing requirements, such as an unlicensed contractor's job. Cash sales under $100 are exempt. The penalty is a fine of at least $1,000 and up to 6 months in county jail.
rules.applies_to: Suppliers, equipment rental firms, subcontractors and service providers selling to contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: it is a misdemeanor to sell equipment, supplies, or services to any person with knowledge that the equipment, supplies, or services are to be used in the performance of a service or contract in violation of the licensing requirements of this code. The provisions of this section shall not be applicable to cash sales of less than one hundred dollars ($100).
rules.notes: The penalty text reads: 'punishable by a fine of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) and by imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding six months.' A supplier tool could verify the buyer's CSLB license on credit accounts and on sales of $100 or more.

rules.title: Board must acknowledge a consumer complaint within 10 days
rules.plain_english: When someone files a complaint against a licensee, the board must tell the complainant what initial action it took within 10 days of receiving it, and later tell them the final action. The board may notify the contractor, ask for relief for the complainant, and mediate. Complaints outside its jurisdiction are referred to the right agency.

board_may: notify licensee of the nature of the complaint
meet and confer with complainant and licensee to mediate
parameters.outside_jurisdiction: complaint and evidence transmitted to the most effective agency; complainant notified

rules.applies_to: Homeowners and others filing CSLB complaints; licensees who are the subject of complaints
rules.verbatim_quote: Each board shall, upon receipt of any complaint respecting an individual licensed by the board, notify the complainant of the initial administrative action taken on the complainant’s complaint within 10 days of receipt. Each board shall notify the complainant of the final action taken on the complainant’s complaint.
rules.notes: Useful for an owner-side complaint tracker (receipt date + 10 days). Board mediation cannot set or modify any fee the licensee charges (129(c)).

verification.note: Not a target category; 10-day period checked.

rules.title: Initial license fees prorated for multi-year license terms
rules.plain_english: When a license term is longer than one year, initial license fees for licenses issued partway through a current license term are prorated by year.

parameters.fee_type: initial license fees for licenses issued during a current license term

rules.applies_to: New license applicants where the board uses fixed multi-year license periods
rules.verbatim_quote: When the term of any license issued by any agency in the department exceeds one year, initial license fees for licenses which are issued during a current license term shall be prorated on a yearly basis.
rules.notes: CSLB's license term and fee amounts are set in Chapter 9 (not in this chunk). Whether CSLB's license terms run per licensee or on a shared cycle determines whether this applies. Verify before building a proration calculator. B&P 7140: CSLB licenses expire 2 years from the last day of the month issued (individual cycle), so 134 proration likely has no practical effect for CSLB.

verification.note: Statute text confirmed. B&P 7140 (PDF page 383) says CSLB licenses expire two years from the last day of the month of issuance, so each license runs on its own cycle. With no shared "current license term", B&P 134 proration likely has no practical effect for CSLB. That is an inference.

rules.title: No extra conditions for retaking a failed exam
rules.plain_english: Failing an exam cannot be used to add extra requirements for retaking it. If you passed part of a divisible exam, you may have to retake those parts if you do not pass all parts within the agency's time limit. Regular exam fees still apply.

parameters.exception: agency may require reexamination of passed parts of a divisible exam if all parts are not passed within the agency's required period

rules.applies_to: Contractor license exam candidates
rules.verbatim_quote: No agency in the department shall, on the basis of an applicant’s failure to successfully complete prior examinations, impose any additional limitations, restrictions, prerequisites, or requirements on any applicant who wishes to participate in subsequent examinations
rules.notes: CSLB's application-validity period and retake rules are in Chapter 9 or regulations (not here).

rules.title: Expedited initial licensure for refugees, asylees and SIV holders
rules.plain_english: CSLB must expedite initial licensing for applicants admitted as refugees, granted asylum, or holding qualifying special immigrant visas. All normal licensing requirements still apply, and this covers individual licenses only.

eligible: special immigrant visa holder under Sec. 1244 of PL 110-181, PL 109-163, or Sec. 602(b) of Title VI, Div. F of PL 111-8
parameters.license_scope: individual license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Refugee, asylee and SIV applicants for an individual license
rules.verbatim_quote: a board within the department shall expedite, and may assist, the initial licensure process for an applicant who supplies satisfactory evidence to the board that they have been admitted to the United States as a refugee
rules.notes: No fee waiver is stated.

rules.title: Report a mailing address change within 30 days
rules.plain_english: Notify CSLB's main office of any change in your mailing address within 30 days, or sooner if a board regulation requires. Failing to do so can bring a citation and fine.

parameters.penalty: citation and administrative fine (where board has citation authority)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and registrants
rules.verbatim_quote: shall notify the issuing board at its principal office of any change in the person’s mailing address within 30 days after the change, unless the board has specified by regulations a shorter time period.
rules.notes: CSLB-specific rule verified: B&P 7083(a) requires written notice within 90 days of any change to recorded information, including business address, "Notwithstanding any other law". Failure is grounds for discipline, and a late change takes effect only on receipt (7083(b)-(c)). B&P 7083.1 sets 90 days for licenses that are expired, suspended (renewable) or cancelled, and requires keeping an address of record for 5 years. Calendar 30 days (B&P 136) for mailing-address changes as the conservative deadline and 90 days for other recorded changes. Board notices go to the last known address (B&P 124).

verification.note: The B&P 136 30-day rule is confirmed. Conflict to flag: CSLB B&P 7083(a) (PDF page 323) requires notice "in writing within 90 days of any change to information recorded under this chapter", expressly including business address, and opens with "Notwithstanding any other law". B&P 7083.1 sets 90 days for address changes on expired, suspended or cancelled licenses. Under 7083(b) a late change takes effect only when received. 30 days is the conservative deadline for a mailing-address change, but the CSLB-specific statute says 90 days.

rules.title: Boards may require license numbers in all advertising
rules.plain_english: A board may require licensees to put their license number in all advertising, solicitations and other public presentations. Ad agencies and media that publish the number exactly as the licensee gave it, or publish none because none was given, are not liable under this section.

parameters.non_licensee_publisher_liability: none for publishing the number exactly as provided by licensee or omitting it if none provided

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees advertising or soliciting work; advertising agencies and publishers
rules.verbatim_quote: Any agency within the department may promulgate regulations requiring licensees to include their license numbers in any advertising, soliciting, or other presentments to the public.
rules.notes: This section only grants authority. The actual contractor rule requiring license numbers on ads, bids and contracts is in Chapter 9 (B&P 7030.5, not in this chunk) and CSLB regulations. An ad and website checker should enforce that rule.

rules.title: Boards had to begin rulemaking (by June 30, 1999) requiring licensees to notify customers they are state-licensed
rules.plain_english: B&P 138 directs each DCA board to start adopting regulations, on or before June 30, 1999, that require its licensees to tell clients or customers that they are licensed by California. A board is exempt if it already has such a consumer-notice requirement in statute or regulation. The section itself does not impose a duty directly on licensees. Any licensee duty comes from the board's own statute or regulation; for CSLB, see Chapter 9 and CSLB regulations.

parameters.notice_content: practitioner is licensed by the State of California
parameters.exemption: board already has a statutory or regulatory consumer notice of licensure requirement
parameters.obligated_party: board (to initiate rulemaking), not licensee directly
parameters.board_obligation: initiate the process of adopting regulations

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.verbatim_quote: Every board in the department, as defined in Section 22, shall initiate the process of adopting regulations on or before June 30, 1999, to require its licensees, as defined in Section 23.8, to provide notice to their clients or customers that the practitioner is licensed by this state.
rules.notes: For contractors, the operative notice requirements (license number and CSLB notices in contracts and ads) are in Chapter 9 and CSLB regulations. This section is the underlying mandate.

verification.correction: The title said "Licensees must tell customers they are state-licensed", and the plain English said boards "had to adopt rules". B&P 138 only requires each board to "initiate the process of adopting regulations" by 6/30/1999, and exempts boards with an existing statutory or regulatory notice requirement. It creates no direct licensee duty. Title and plain_english were rescoped, and obligated_party and board_obligation parameters were added. The quote is accurate.

rules.title: Keep records of cash wage payments for at least 3 years
rules.plain_english: You must record, and keep for at least 3 years, every cash transaction used to pay employee wages, and make those records available to the board's representatives. Failing to do either is grounds for discipline.

parameters.records_required: all cash transactions involved in payment of employee wages

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees with employees, especially those paying any wages in cash
rules.verbatim_quote: may take disciplinary action upon the ground that the licensee has failed to record and preserve for not less than three years, any and all cash transactions involved in the payment of employee wages by a licensee. Failure to make these records available to an authorized representative of the board may be made grounds for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: A payroll or records tool can set a 3-year minimum retention lock on cash payroll records. Labor and tax law may require longer retention.

verification.note: Not a target category; 3-year retention checked.

rules.title: Cash-wage records violation: up to $2,500 in investigative costs
rules.plain_english: If the board proves a cash-wage recordkeeping violation, it can charge you its actual investigative costs up to $2,500. Not paying those costs can lead to license revocation.

parameters.trigger: action brought and sustained by board for violation of B&P 140 or its regulations
parameters.failure_to_pay_consequence: may result in revocation of the license

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees found in violation of B&P 140
rules.verbatim_quote: In any action brought and sustained by the board which involves a violation of this section and any regulation adopted thereto, the board may assess the licensee with the actual investigative costs incurred, not to exceed two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500). Failure to pay those costs may result in revocation of the license.

rules.title: Out-of-state, federal or foreign discipline can trigger California discipline
rules.plain_english: Discipline taken against you by another state, a federal agency, or another country for conduct substantially related to contracting can be grounds for CSLB discipline. A certified copy of that record is conclusive evidence of what it describes.

disciplining_sources: any agency of the federal government
parameters.nexus_required: act substantially related to the practice regulated by the California license
parameters.evidence: certified copy of the disciplinary record is conclusive evidence

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees also licensed or regulated elsewhere
rules.verbatim_quote: a disciplinary action taken by another state, by any agency of the federal government, or by another country for any act substantially related to the practice regulated by the California license, may be a ground for disciplinary action by the respective state licensing board.
rules.notes: A multi-state contractor compliance tool should track out-of-state license actions as a California risk.

verification.note: Confirmed. B&P 141(b) preserves any board-specific statute on discipline based on out-of-state actions.

rules.title: No lawsuit for payment unless licensed at all times during the work
rules.plain_english: You cannot sue to collect payment for work that requires a license unless you allege and prove you were properly licensed the entire time you performed the work or contract, no matter how strong your claim is. Substantial compliance is not enough. The only exception is the B&P 121 period while a timely renewal is being processed.

parameters.must_allege_and_prove: duly licensed at all times during performance of the act or contract
parameters.exception: act or contract qualifying as lawful practice under B&P 121 (timely renewal pending)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors seeking to collect payment in court; owners defending collection suits
rules.verbatim_quote: No person engaged in any business or profession for which a license is required ... may bring or maintain any action ... for the collection of compensation ... without alleging and proving that he or she was duly licensed at all times during the performance of that act or contract ... (b) The judicial doctrine of substantial compliance shall not apply to this section.
rules.notes: The contractor-specific version is B&P 7031 (Chapter 9, not in this chunk), which also allows owners to recover payments made to unlicensed contractors. A tool should log daily license status (active, correct classification, not suspended) for every day of the project, and flag any lapse before invoicing or lien and collection steps.

rules.title: Settlements cannot bar complaints to CSLB
rules.plain_english: A settlement agreement cannot bar the other side (for example a homeowner) from contacting, complaining to, or cooperating with CSLB, and cannot require them to withdraw a CSLB complaint. Such a clause is void, and a contractor who includes it, or lets an agent include it, can be disciplined. This applies whether or not a lawsuit has been filed.

prohibited_clauses: prohibits the other party from contacting the board
prohibits the other party from filing a complaint with the board
prohibits the other party from cooperating with the board
requires the other party to withdraw a complaint from the board
parameters.agreement_types: agreements to settle a civil dispute, before or after a civil action is commenced
covered_parties: entity or person acting as authorized agent of the licensee
parameters.exemptions: only causes of action exempted by board regulation adopted on petition under 143.5(d)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and their attorneys or agents drafting settlement or release agreements with owners, customers or others
rules.verbatim_quote: No licensee who is regulated by a board ... shall include or permit to be included a provision in an agreement to settle a civil dispute ... that prohibits the other party in that dispute from contacting, filing a complaint with, or cooperating with the department, board, bureau, or program ... A provision of that nature is void as against public policy
rules.notes: A document checker can scan settlement, release and NDA drafts for language that restricts contact with CSLB or DCA or requires withdrawing a complaint, and block it.

rules.title: No extra board-ordered payments to a plaintiff after a full civil settlement
rules.plain_english: If a complaint was also the subject of a civil lawsuit that settled for money in full and final satisfaction, the board can still discipline you but cannot make you pay additional amounts to that plaintiff.

conditions: board discipline based on a complaint or report that was also the subject of a civil action
civil action settled for monetary damages providing full and final satisfaction of the parties

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees who settled a civil suit that also generated a CSLB complaint
rules.verbatim_quote: Any board, bureau, or program within the Department of Consumer Affairs that takes disciplinary action against a licensee or licensees based on a complaint or report that has also been the subject of a civil action and that has been settled for monetary damages providing for full and final satisfaction of the parties may not require its licensee or licensees to pay any additional sums
rules.notes: Settlement documents should state full and final satisfaction clearly to get this protection. Cost recovery or fines payable to the board are a separate matter.

rules.title: CSLB applicants must submit fingerprints
rules.plain_english: CSLB must require applicants to submit a full set of fingerprints for criminal history checks. CSLB may get criminal history from the California DOJ and the FBI.
rules.applies_to: CSLB license applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: an agency designated in subdivision (b) shall require an applicant to furnish to the agency a full set of fingerprints for purposes of conducting criminal history record checks. ... (23) Contractors State License Board.
rules.notes: Which individuals on an entity application must be fingerprinted (e.g., officers, qualifiers) is set by CSLB rules in Chapter 9 or regulations, not this section. Add Live Scan fingerprinting as a step in an application checklist.

rules.title: Boards may shift renewal dates by up to 6 months, with fees prorated
rules.plain_english: With the DCA Director's approval, a board may extend the legal renewal date of a license by up to 6 months to spread out renewal work. Any renewal fee is prorated so you pay neither more nor less than you otherwise would.

parameters.fee_adjustment: prorated so no greater or lesser fee than without the change

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees with renewal dates
rules.verbatim_quote: the boards in the department may, with the approval of the director, extend by not more than six months the date fixed by law for the renewal of any license, certificate or permit issued by them, except that in such event any renewal fee which may be involved shall be prorated
rules.notes: A license tracker should take the expiration date from the actual CSLB record rather than computing it from the issue date, because boards can set and shift license periods (152.6).

verification.note: Quote matches across the page break, which caused the automated match to miss.

verification_summary.method: Each target rule (deadline, money_amount, threshold, penalty, required_notice; no threshold or required_contract_clause rules exist in this file) was read against the full section text in sources/lawbook.txt (PDF page = form-feed page index), and CSLB Chapter 9 counterparts were checked where the DCA default may be displaced. Six numeric process_step/required_document rules were also checked.
